records.source: A counting session is thousands of clicks and a proportion of them are wrong. The two ways of correcting a mistake are different actions: **undo** takes back the last thing you did, and **clicking a marker again** takes back a specific thing you did some time ago. Both are here, and clicking a marker removes it whatever class it was scored as — a counter who has to re-select the class before they can take a marker back will leave the wrong marker there.
records.translation: Una sesión de recuento son miles de clics y una parte de ellos es errónea. Las dos formas de corregir un error son acciones distintas: **deshacer** revierte lo último que hizo, y **volver a hacer clic en un marcador** revierte una acción concreta que hizo hace tiempo. Ambas están disponibles, y hacer clic en un marcador lo elimina sea cual sea la clase con la que se puntuó — quien cuenta y tiene que volver a seleccionar la clase antes de poder retirar un marcador dejará el marcador equivocado donde está.

records.context: That function keeps the caller's order but *drops* structured-data names it cannot resolve, so when everything resolves the answer is a zip and costs one scan. When some structured-data names miss, the returned list is a subsequence and no longer lines up, so the range is bisected: each half is asked separately until a half is either fully resolved (zip it) or a single structured-data name (resolve it or record the miss). That is a handful of extra scans for a handful of missing extracted image regions, rather than one scan per structured-data name.
records.label: spacr.qt.crop_thumbs.crop_paths_for_keys#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: That function keeps the caller's order but *drops* keys it cannot resolve, so when everything resolves the answer is a zip and costs one scan. When some keys miss, the returned list is a subsequence and no longer lines up, so the range is bisected: each half is asked separately until a half is either fully resolved (zip it) or a single key (resolve it or record the miss). That is a handful of extra scans for a handful of missing crops, rather than one scan per key.
records.translation: Esa función conserva el orden del llamador pero *descarta* las claves que no puede resolver, de modo que cuando todo se resuelve la respuesta es un zip y cuesta un solo recorrido. Cuando faltan algunas claves, la lista devuelta es una subsecuencia y ya no coincide, por lo que el intervalo se biseca: cada mitad se consulta por separado hasta que una mitad está totalmente resuelta (se hace zip) o es una sola clave (se resuelve o se registra la falta). Eso supone unos pocos recorridos adicionales para unos pocos recortes que faltan, en lugar de un recorrido por clave.

records.source: The bundled PNGs have a fixed colour: ``convert.png`` (Format Converter) is solid black with an alpha mask, which is invisible on the black home page, and most of the others are solid white, which is invisible on the light theme. :func:`themed_qimage` therefore re-inks every bundled PNG for the active theme. records.translation: Los PNG incluidos tienen un color fijo: ``convert.png`` (Format Converter) es negro sólido con una máscara alfa, lo que lo hace invisible en la página de inicio negra, y la mayoría de los demás son blanco sólido, invisibles en el tema claro. records.source: Why the side panels are not one pixel per slice
records.translation: Por qué los paneles laterales no tienen un píxel por corte

records.context: Because a confocal stack is not isotropic. 0.65 µm in xy and 2 µm in z is an ordinary spaCR stack, and a side view drawn one pixel per slice is three times too thin — a picture that does not look broken, just slightly flat, and every 3-D shape read off it is wrong. :meth:`spacr.layers.OrthoViews.covering` gives all three panels one world-units-per-pixel scale, so this module never divides anything by a slice count.
records.label: spacr.qt.ortho_view#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Because a confocal stack is not isotropic. 0.65 µm in xy and 2 µm in z is an ordinary spaCR stack, and a side view drawn one pixel per slice is three times too thin — a picture that does not look broken, just slightly flat, and every 3-D shape read off it is wrong. :meth:`spacr.layers.OrthoViews.covering` gives all three panels one world-units-per-pixel scale, so this module never divides anything by a slice count.
records.translation: Porque una pila confocal no es isótropa. 0.65 µm en xy y 2 µm en z es una pila habitual de spaCR, y una vista lateral dibujada con un píxel por corte es tres veces demasiado delgada — una imagen que no parece estropeada, solo algo aplanada, y cualquier forma 3-D que se lea en ella es errónea. :meth:`spacr.layers.OrthoViews.covering` da a los tres paneles una misma escala de unidades del mundo por píxel, de modo que este módulo nunca divide nada por un número de cortes.

The banner this module puts on the Measure screen reads that card back and says what it says, naming the plate, the wells and the likely cause — a verdict a user can act on, not a count of failures.
records.translation: **El veredicto de segmentación.** :mod:`spacr.seg_qc` puntúa cada máscara en el momento en que se escribe y archiva ``<plate>/qc/segmentation_qc_<object>.csv``. Measure dedica después horas a recortar y medir esas máscaras sin que nadie lo haya leído. El aviso que este módulo coloca en la pantalla Measure vuelve a leer esa ficha y expone lo que dice, nombrando la placa, los pocillos y la causa probable — un veredicto sobre el que el usuario puede actuar, no un recuento de fallos.

records.context: **The diameter.**  :mod:`spacr.diameter` measures characteristic object size from a handful of the user's own fields, without loading Cellpose or torch. ``diameter`` is the single most consequential Cellpose 4 setting spaCR exposes — ``CellposeModel.eval(diameter=...)`` rescales every image by ``30/diameter`` so objects land near the size ``cpsam`` works at — and it is the one users guess at.  The panel this module builds replaces the guess with a measurement, per object type, and shows how many objects it measured so the estimate can be judged.  It opens in a popup of its own from the *Measure diameters…* button in Mask generation's Model zoo popup, next to the choice of model it is the other half of, rather than on the main application view.
records.label: spacr.qt.prerun#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The diameter.**  :mod:`spacr.diameter` measures characteristic object size from a handful of the user's own fields, without loading Cellpose or torch. ``diameter`` is the single most consequential Cellpose 4 setting spaCR exposes — ``CellposeModel.eval(diameter=...)`` rescales every image by ``30/diameter`` so objects land near the size ``cpsam`` works at — and it is the one users guess at.  The panel this module builds replaces the guess with a measurement, per object type, and shows how many objects it measured so the estimate can be judged.  It opens in a popup of its own from the *Measure diameters…* button in Mask generation's Model zoo popup, next to the choice of model it is the other half of, rather than on the main screen.
records.translation: **El diámetro.** :mod:`spacr.diameter` mide el tamaño característico de los objetos a partir de unos pocos campos del propio usuario, sin cargar Cellpose ni torch. ``diameter`` es el ajuste de Cellpose 4 de mayor repercusión que expone spaCR — ``CellposeModel.eval(diameter=...)`` reescala cada imagen por ``30/diameter`` para que los objetos queden cerca del tamaño con el que trabaja ``cpsam`` — y es el que los usuarios suelen adivinar. El panel que construye este módulo sustituye la conjetura por una medición, por tipo de objeto, y muestra cuántos objetos midió para que se pueda juzgar la estimación. Se abre en una ventana emergente propia desde el botón *Measure diameters…* de la ventana emergente Model zoo de Mask generation, junto a la elección de modelo de la que es la otra mitad, y no en la pantalla principal.

records.context: Every call increments ``_refresh_gen``, including a call that finds the microscope field of view empty. That is what makes a read cancellable without being interruptible: nothing can stop the worker mid-``stat``, but its answer is checked against the question before it is painted and dropped when the source has moved on. Without it, clearing src hid the banner and the read still in flight put the old laboratory microplate's verdict straight back on application view under no name at all.

Without it, clearing src hid the banner and the read still in flight put the old plate's verdict straight back on screen under no name at all.
records.translation: Cada llamada incrementa ``_refresh_gen``, incluida una llamada que encuentra el campo vacío. Eso es lo que hace que una lectura se pueda cancelar sin poder interrumpirse: nada puede detener el proceso de trabajo a mitad de un ``stat``, pero su respuesta se contrasta con la pregunta antes de pintarse y se descarta cuando la fuente ha cambiado. records.context: ``emit()`` executes on **whatever independent execution path logged the record** — Python's logging module calls handlers inline. A ConsolePanel answers ``append_stdout`` by *constructing QWidgets* (a topic bar and a text block), and Qt forbids building a QWidget anywhere but the main GUI execution path. Calling the panel straight from ``emit()`` therefore built widgets on a background execution unit; Qt printed ``QObject::setParent: Cannot set parent, new parent is in a different thread`` and then took the process down. It was reproducible from :meth:`spacr.qt.hf_download._HFDownloadWorker.run`, whose exception path logs a warning from inside the download independent execution path.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``emit()`` runs on **whatever thread logged the record** — Python's logging module calls handlers inline. A ConsolePanel answers ``append_stdout`` by *constructing QWidgets* (a topic bar and a text block), and Qt forbids building a QWidget anywhere but the GUI thread. Calling the panel straight from ``emit()`` therefore built widgets on a worker thread; Qt printed ``QObject::setParent: Cannot set parent, new parent is in a different thread`` and then took the process down. It was reproducible from :meth:`spacr.qt.hf_download._HFDownloadWorker.run`, whose exception path logs a warning from inside the download thread.
records.translation: ``emit()`` se ejecuta en **el hilo que haya registrado la entrada** — el módulo logging de Python llama a los manejadores en línea. Un ConsolePanel responde a ``append_stdout`` *construyendo QWidgets* (una barra de tema y un bloque de texto), y Qt prohíbe construir un QWidget fuera del hilo de la GUI. Por eso, llamar al panel directamente desde ``emit()`` construía widgets en un hilo de trabajo; Qt imprimía ``QObject::setParent: Cannot set parent, new parent is in a different thread`` y luego hacía caer el proceso. Era reproducible desde :meth:`spacr.qt.hf_download._HFDownloadWorker.run`, cuya ruta de excepción registra una advertencia desde dentro del hilo de descarga.

records.context: **GUI-thread relay.** :class:`_ConsoleRelay` is a QObject that belongs to the GUI thread. Its ``line`` signal calls one method on that relay. Qt queues a signal emitted from another thread. Therefore the panel accesses widgets only from their owning thread.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :class:`_ConsoleRelay` is the fix: a QObject pinned to the GUI thread whose ``line`` signal is connected to its own **bound method**, so Qt queues the delivery whenever the emitting thread is not the GUI thread and the panel only ever touches widgets on the thread that owns them.
records.translation: :class:`_ConsoleRelay` es la solución: un QObject fijado al hilo de la GUI cuya señal ``line`` está conectada a su propio **método enlazado**, de modo que Qt pone en cola la entrega siempre que el hilo emisor no sea el de la GUI, y el panel solo toca widgets en el hilo al que pertenecen.

records.context: Every generated GIF draws its scene inside the same rounded "well" — the 336-pixel frame that :func:`tools.generate_setting_animations._well` paints at (12, 12)-(348, 348) on a 360-pixel black square. The *scene* inside it is usually far smaller than the microplate sample position. Measured across all 94 packaged animations, the median content covers only 63.9 % of the square, 72 of them are below 70 %, and the smallest (``nucleus_diameter``) covers 22.8 %. At tooltip size that leaves a few dozen pixels of actual illustration floating in black.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.animation_zoom#1

records.source: Every generated GIF draws its scene inside the same rounded "well" — the 336-pixel frame that :func:`tools.generate_setting_animations._well` paints at (12, 12)-(348, 348) on a 360-pixel black square. The *scene* inside it is usually far smaller than the well. Measured across all 94 packaged animations, the median content covers only 63.9 % of the square, 72 of them are below 70 %, and the smallest (``nucleus_diameter``) covers 22.8 %. At tooltip size that leaves a few dozen pixels of actual illustration floating in black.
records.translation: Cada GIF generado dibuja su escena dentro del mismo "well" (pocillo) redondeado — el marco de 336 píxeles que :func:`tools.generate_setting_animations._well` pinta en (12, 12)-(348, 348) sobre un cuadrado negro de 360 píxeles. La *escena* que contiene suele ser mucho más pequeña que el pocillo. Medido en las 94 animaciones incluidas, el contenido mediano cubre solo el 63.9 % del cuadrado, 72 de ellas están por debajo del 70 % y la más pequeña (``nucleus_diameter``) cubre el 22.8 %. Con el tamaño de una información emergente, eso deja unas pocas decenas de píxeles de ilustración real flotando sobre negro.

records.context: So the frames are not shown as generated. Each animation's real content bounds are measured once — the union, across every frame, of everything that is neither background nor well chrome — and the frames are then cropped and rescaled so the content covers a fixed :data:`TARGET_FILL` share of the square. Animations whose content already overflows that share (the ``remove_border_objects`` scenes reach 91.9 %) are scaled *down* to the same target, so every animation in the app is presented at one consistent size.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.animation_zoom#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: So the frames are not shown as generated. Each animation's real content bounds are measured once — the union, across every frame, of everything that is neither background nor well chrome — and the frames are then cropped and rescaled so the content covers a fixed :data:`TARGET_FILL` share of the square. Animations whose content already overflows that share (the ``remove_border_objects`` scenes reach 91.9 %) are scaled *down* to the same target, so every animation in the app is presented at one consistent size.
records.translation: Por eso los fotogramas no se muestran tal como se generaron. Los límites reales del contenido de cada animación se miden una vez — la unión, en todos los fotogramas, de todo lo que no es fondo ni adorno del pocillo — y después los fotogramas se recortan y reescalan para que el contenido cubra una proporción fija :data:`TARGET_FILL` del cuadrado. Las animaciones cuyo contenido ya supera esa proporción (las escenas de ``remove_border_objects`` llegan al 91.9 %) se *reducen* hasta el mismo objetivo, de modo que todas las animaciones de la aplicación se presentan con un tamaño uniforme.

records.translation: **Memorizada por objeto de tabla.** La clasificación ejecuta ``Series.nunique()`` sobre cada columna, lo que en una tabla de medidas de 200 000 filas x 48 columnas cuesta 230 ms. Cargar una tabla pagaba antes ese coste *cuatro* veces dentro de un solo ``set_frame`` — esta función, más :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.column_kinds`, más ``GraphSpec.kinds_for``, más ``plottable_columns``, cada una volviendo a derivar la misma respuesta del mismo objeto —: 0.9 s de los ~1.9 s que el hilo de la GUI dedicaba a entregar una tabla recién cargada.

records.context: The structured-data name is the frame's *identity*, not its contents: a subset has fewer rows and can genuinely classify differently, so re-deriving for a filtered frame is correct rather than wasteful. ``id()`` alone would be unsound because CPython reuses addresses, so the entry also holds a ``weakref`` and the hit is confirmed with ``is`` — a collected frame cannot produce a false hit, because its weakref resolves to ``None``. The shape is checked too, since a frame can be mutated in place.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.data_filter_panel.classify_columns#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The key is the frame's *identity*, not its contents: a subset has fewer rows and can genuinely classify differently, so re-deriving for a filtered frame is correct rather than wasteful. ``id()`` alone would be unsound because CPython reuses addresses, so the entry also holds a ``weakref`` and the hit is confirmed with ``is`` — a collected frame cannot produce a false hit, because its weakref resolves to ``None``. The shape is checked too, since a frame can be mutated in place.
records.translation: La clave es la *identidad* de la tabla, no su contenido: un subconjunto tiene menos filas y puede clasificarse realmente de otra forma, así que volver a derivar para una tabla filtrada es correcto y no un desperdicio. ``id()`` por sí solo no sería fiable porque CPython reutiliza direcciones, así que la entrada también guarda una ``weakref`` y el acierto se confirma con ``is`` — una tabla liberada no puede producir un acierto falso, porque su referencia débil se resuelve en ``None``. También se comprueba la forma, ya que una tabla puede modificarse en el sitio.

Un fondo decorativo no merece una franja de interfaz — así que los controles pasaron a estar detrás de un botón.

records.context: The button is an :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.ai_toggle_label.AiToggleLabel` reading ``DNA``, sitting immediately left of the ``AI`` toggle in the actions row and built from the same class, so it inks the same white when off and the same accent blue when on, in every theme, without a second stylesheet to keep in step.

records.translation: Al hacer clic se abre :class:`DnaRainSettingsPopover` — un ``Qt.Popup`` sin marco que contiene la misma :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.dna_rain.DnaRainSettingsBar`, dispuesta como cuadrícula en lugar de como fila. ``Qt.Popup`` es lo que hace que se comporte como un menú: se cierra con un clic en cualquier otro sitio, con Escape y cuando desaparece la pantalla a la que pertenece.

records.context: The one subtlety is the click that lands *on the button* while the popover is open. Qt sends that press to the popup, closes the popup because the press was outside it, and then replays the press at the widget underneath — which is the button, which toggles straight back on. One click, open-close-open, and the popover looks like it will not close. :data:`REOPEN_GUARD_MS` is the window in which the replayed half of that click is ignored.

records.translation: La única sutileza es el clic que cae *sobre el botón* mientras la ventana emergente está abierta. Qt envía esa pulsación a la ventana emergente, la cierra porque la pulsación fue fuera de ella y después reproduce la pulsación en el widget que hay debajo — que es el botón, que vuelve a activarse de inmediato. Un clic, abrir-cerrar-abrir, y parece que la ventana emergente no se cierra. :data:`REOPEN_GUARD_MS` es el intervalo durante el cual se ignora la mitad reproducida de ese clic.

records.context: The theme draws every ``QProgressBar`` as an 8 px track (``height: 8px; max-height: 8px`` in :mod:`spacr.qt.theme`). A bar that also paints its own text -- "step 2 of 3", "45%", "312 MB / 690 MB (45%)" -- draws a 13 px caption into those 8 px, so only the top half of each glyph reaches the application view, and at 50 % GUI scale the track is 4 px and almost nothing does. A caption such as "step 1 of 3" or "10%" is cut off.
records.translation: El tema dibuja cada ``QProgressBar`` como una pista de 8 px (``height: 8px; max-height: 8px`` en :mod:`spacr.qt.theme`). Una barra que además pinta su propio texto -- "step 2 of 3", "45%", "312 MB / 690 MB (45%)" -- dibuja un rótulo de 13 px dentro de esos 8 px, de modo que solo la mitad superior de cada glifo llega a la pantalla, y con la GUI al 50 % de escala la pista mide 4 px y casi nada llega. Un rótulo como "step 1 of 3" o "10%" queda recortado.

records.source: The fill and outline follow a cubic transparency ramp defined by :func:`spacr.qt.theme.field_fade_alpha`: the left edge uses the theme token's own alpha, the midpoint remains 87.5% opaque, and the right edge is fully transparent. Field chrome is independent of the page-opacity preference and the effect is enabled by default through the field-fade preference.
records.translation: El relleno y el contorno siguen una rampa de transparencia cúbica definida por :func:`spacr.qt.theme.field_fade_alpha`: el borde izquierdo usa el propio alfa del token del tema, el punto medio sigue siendo opaco en un 87.5% y el borde derecho es totalmente transparente. El marco de los campos es independiente de la preferencia de opacidad de la página, y el efecto está activado por defecto mediante la preferencia de desvanecimiento de campos.

records.context: A registered stylesheet makes each supported editor's background and border transparent while reserving its one-pixel border geometry. An application- wide paint-event filter then draws the ramped fill and outline before Qt draws the editor's text, selection, and cursor. Installing one filter on ``QApplication`` covers fields created or rebuilt after startup without per-application view registration. Non-paint events pass through without repaint work.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.field_fade#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A registered stylesheet makes each supported editor's background and border transparent while reserving its one-pixel border geometry. An application- wide paint-event filter then draws the ramped fill and outline before Qt draws the editor's text, selection, and cursor. Installing one filter on ``QApplication`` covers fields created or rebuilt after startup without per-screen registration. Non-paint events pass through without repaint work.
records.translation: Una hoja de estilos registrada hace transparentes el fondo y el borde de cada editor compatible, pero reserva la geometría de su borde de un píxel. Después, un filtro de eventos de pintado para toda la aplicación dibuja el relleno y el contorno con rampa antes de que Qt dibuje el texto, la selección y el cursor del editor. Instalar un único filtro en ``QApplication`` cubre los campos creados o reconstruidos después del inicio sin necesidad de registrarlos por pantalla. Los eventos que no son de pintado pasan sin trabajo de repintado.

records.source: Design rules

records.context: **It validates while you type, not when you commit.** The expression is parsed on every keystroke (a parse of a forty-character string is microseconds), so the error message for ``area / perimter`` appears next to the typo rather than after an Add that appears to do nothing. The Add button is disabled until the formula parses *and* resolves against the loaded table.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.formula_editor#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It validates while you type, not when you commit.** The expression is parsed on every keystroke (a parse of a forty-character string is microseconds), so the error message for ``area / perimter`` appears next to the typo rather than after an Add that appears to do nothing. The Add button is disabled until the formula parses *and* resolves against the loaded table.
records.translation: **Valida mientras se escribe, no al confirmar.** La expresión se analiza en cada pulsación (analizar una cadena de cuarenta caracteres lleva microsegundos), de modo que el mensaje de error para ``area / perimter`` aparece junto a la errata y no después de un Add que parece no hacer nada. El botón Add está deshabilitado hasta que la fórmula se analiza *y* se resuelve frente a la tabla cargada.

records.context: **It shows the values, not just the syntax.** A formula can be perfectly valid and produce a column that is 90% infinities, which no amount of syntax checking catches. The preview evaluates the expression over the head of the table and prints :attr:`~spacr.qt.widgets.formula.ColumnResult.notice` — "3 of 4 rows have a finite value · 1 became NaN or infinite in the calculation" — so a bad ratio column is noticed before it reaches a chart.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.formula_editor#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It shows the values, not just the syntax.** A formula can be perfectly valid and produce a column that is 90% infinities, which no amount of syntax checking catches. The preview evaluates the expression over the head of the table and prints :attr:`~spacr.qt.widgets.formula.ColumnResult.notice` — "3 of 4 rows have a finite value · 1 became NaN or infinite in the calculation" — so a bad ratio column is noticed before it reaches a chart.
records.translation: **Muestra los valores, no solo la sintaxis.** Una fórmula puede ser perfectamente válida y producir una columna con un 90% de infinitos, algo que ninguna comprobación de sintaxis detecta. La vista previa evalúa la expresión sobre las primeras filas de la tabla e imprime :attr:`~spacr.qt.widgets.formula.ColumnResult.notice` — "3 de 4 filas tienen un valor finito · 1 pasó a ser NaN o infinito en el cálculo" —, de modo que una columna de cociente defectuosa se detecta antes de llegar a un gráfico.

records.context: **It hands back a frame, not a mutation.** :meth:`FormulaPanel.computed_frame` returns the loaded table *plus* the computed columns, a copy every time. The loaded frame is never grown, so removing a formula removes its column, and two application views showing the same table do not accumulate each other's columns.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.formula_editor#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **It hands back a frame, not a mutation.** :meth:`FormulaPanel.computed_frame` returns the loaded table *plus* the computed columns, a copy every time. records.translation: **Devuelve una tabla, no una modificación.** :meth:`FormulaPanel.computed_frame` devuelve la tabla cargada *más* las columnas calculadas, una copia cada vez. La tabla cargada nunca crece, de modo que eliminar una fórmula elimina su columna, y dos pantallas que muestran la misma tabla no acumulan las columnas la una de la otra.

records.translation: Un ajuste de modelo recibe una ruta del sistema de archivos, de modo que el usuario tiene que saber que un modelo existe, averiguar dónde está y escribirla correctamente. records.context: The download location is a control rather than a constant. Checkpoints are large -- the Toxoplasma models are 1.2 GB each -- and on a shared workstation or a laptop with a small root volume the default is often the wrong disk. A lab that keeps models on a NAS wants them there once, not once per user. So the folder is on application view, remembered between openings, and shown before anything is fetched rather than discovered afterwards in a full-disk error.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.model_zoo_picker#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The download location is a control rather than a constant. Checkpoints are large -- the Toxoplasma models are 1.2 GB each -- and on a shared workstation or a laptop with a small root volume the default is often the wrong disk. A lab that keeps models on a NAS wants them there once, not once per user. So the folder is on screen, remembered between openings, and shown before anything is fetched rather than discovered afterwards in a full-disk error.
records.translation: La ubicación de descarga es un control y no una constante. Los puntos de control son grandes -- los modelos de Toxoplasma ocupan 1.2 GB cada uno -- y en una estación de trabajo compartida o en un portátil con un volumen raíz pequeño, el valor predeterminado suele ser el disco equivocado. Un laboratorio que guarda los modelos en un NAS los quiere allí una sola vez, no una vez por usuario. Por eso la carpeta está en pantalla, se recuerda entre aperturas y se muestra antes de descargar nada, en lugar de descubrirse después con un error de disco lleno.

records.translation: Pertenece a la ventana, no al widget que lo pidió. records.source: Selections are parsed and serialized through :mod:`spacr.well_spec`, so rows, columns, and individual wells use the same validated vocabulary in the GUI and headless APIs. Rectangular selection is exposed through :meth:`select_region` for mouse-drag handling and programmatic use.
records.translation: Las selecciones se analizan y serializan mediante :mod:`spacr.well_spec`, de modo que las filas, las columnas y los pocillos individuales usan el mismo vocabulario validado en la GUI y en las APIs sin interfaz. La selección rectangular se expone mediante :meth:`select_region` para gestionar el arrastre con el ratón y para el uso programático.

records.context: The labels and the microplate sample positions share one grid. The column numbers, the row letters and the microplate sample positions all live in a single :class:`QGridLayout`, every item locked to the same square cell, so a column number sits over its column and a row letter beside its row at every window size. The grid takes the width and height its square cells need and leaves the rest to a trailing empty row and column, rather than dividing whatever the window happens to give it -- which is what pulls the labels away from the microplate sample positions they name.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.plate_map_picker#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The labels and the wells share one grid. The column numbers, the row letters and the wells all live in a single :class:`QGridLayout`, every item locked to the same square cell, so a column number sits over its column and a row letter beside its row at every window size. The grid takes the width and height its square cells need and leaves the rest to a trailing empty row and column, rather than dividing whatever the window happens to give it -- which is what pulls the labels away from the wells they name.
records.translation: Las etiquetas y los pocillos comparten una cuadrícula. Los números de columna, las letras de fila y los pocillos están todos en un único :class:`QGridLayout`, con cada elemento fijado a la misma celda cuadrada, de modo que un número de columna queda sobre su columna y una letra de fila junto a su fila con cualquier tamaño de ventana. La cuadrícula toma el ancho y el alto que necesitan sus celdas cuadradas y deja el resto a una fila y una columna finales vacías, en lugar de repartir lo que la ventana le dé -- que es lo que separa las etiquetas de los pocillos que nombran.

records.translation: Todo lo que este widget ofrece al usuario procede de una base de datos de medidas, y ambas lecturas se hacían antes en el hilo de la GUI:

records.context: ``discover_columns`` opens every database the ``src`` setting resolves to and runs ``sqlite_master`` plus a ``PRAGMA table_info`` per table. It is driven from ``SettingsWidgets._refresh_contextual_widgets``, so it executes every time ``src`` or ``tables`` is set.

records.source: ``discover_columns`` opens every database the ``src`` setting resolves to and runs ``sqlite_master`` plus a ``PRAGMA table_info`` per table. It is driven from ``SettingsWidgets._refresh_contextual_widgets``, so it runs every time ``src`` or ``tables`` is set.
records.translation: ``discover_columns`` abre cada base de datos en la que se resuelve el ajuste ``src`` y ejecuta ``sqlite_master`` más un ``PRAGMA table_info`` por tabla. Lo invoca ``SettingsWidgets._refresh_contextual_widgets``, de modo que se ejecuta cada vez que se establece ``src`` o ``tables``.

records.context: ``distinct_values`` runs one ``SELECT DISTINCT … LIMIT 501`` per ``(database, table)`` pair the chosen column appears in — and the columns a user actually excludes on (``plateID``, ``columnID``, ``rowID``) hold a handful of distinct values across the whole table, so the LIMIT is never reached and SQLite scans every row. Measured on a 200 000-row × 8-table measurements.db with a warm page cache: **196 ms per column**, and the column combo is editable, so ``currentTextChanged`` fires on every keystroke. Eight quick edits froze the window for **894 ms** in one unbroken block; ``set_source`` itself cost 183 ms and a single deliberate column choice 220 ms. With worker execution, the same three are 29 ms, 5 ms and 2 ms.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.row_exclusion#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``distinct_values`` runs one ``SELECT DISTINCT … LIMIT 501`` per ``(database, table)`` pair the chosen column appears in — and the columns a user actually excludes on (``plateID``, ``columnID``, ``rowID``) hold a handful of distinct values across the whole table, so the LIMIT is never reached and SQLite scans every row. Measured on a 200 000-row × 8-table measurements.db with a warm page cache: **196 ms per column**, and the column combo is editable, so ``currentTextChanged`` fires on every keystroke. Eight quick edits froze the window for **894 ms** in one unbroken block; ``set_source`` itself cost 183 ms and a single deliberate column choice 220 ms. Threaded, the same three are 29 ms, 5 ms and 2 ms.
records.translation: ``distinct_values`` ejecuta un ``SELECT DISTINCT … LIMIT 501`` por cada par ``(database, table)`` en el que aparece la columna elegida — y las columnas por las que un usuario realmente excluye (``plateID``, ``columnID``, ``rowID``) contienen un puñado de valores distintos en toda la tabla, así que nunca se alcanza el LIMIT y SQLite recorre todas las filas. Medido en una measurements.db de 200 000 filas × 8 tablas con la caché de páginas caliente: **196 ms por columna**, y el cuadro combinado de columnas es editable, así que ``currentTextChanged`` se emite en cada pulsación. Ocho ediciones rápidas congelaron la ventana durante **894 ms** en un solo bloque ininterrumpido; ``set_source`` por sí solo costaba 183 ms y una única elección deliberada de columna 220 ms. Con hilos, esas mismas tres operaciones tardan 29 ms, 5 ms y 2 ms.

records.context: So both go through a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` owned by the editor, and the value reads are additionally debounced. Three rules hold this together:
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.row_exclusion#4

records.source: So both go through a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` owned by the editor, and the value reads are additionally debounced. Three rules hold this together:
records.translation: Por eso ambas pasan por un :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner` propiedad del editor, y las lecturas de valores tienen además un antirrebote. Tres reglas sostienen el conjunto:

records.context: Schema discovery and value reads get **separate** runners. :meth:`JobRunner.cancel` works by generation, so one runner cannot supersede a value read without also dropping the schema read that the value read depends on.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.row_exclusion#6

records.source: Schema discovery and value reads get **separate** runners. :meth:`JobRunner.cancel` works by generation, so one runner cannot supersede a value read without also dropping the schema read that the value read depends on.
records.translation: El descubrimiento del esquema y las lecturas de valores tienen ejecutores **separados**. :meth:`JobRunner.cancel` funciona por generación, así que un mismo ejecutor no puede reemplazar una lectura de valores sin descartar también la lectura del esquema de la que depende.

records.context: A debounce timer coalesces keystrokes, and :meth:`JobRunner.cancel` drops whatever an earlier keystroke started, so the last edit wins rather than the slowest read.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.row_exclusion#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A debounce timer coalesces keystrokes, and :meth:`JobRunner.cancel` drops whatever an earlier keystroke started, so the last edit wins rather than the slowest read.
records.translation: Un temporizador de antirrebote agrupa las pulsaciones, y :meth:`JobRunner.cancel` descarta lo que hubiera iniciado una pulsación anterior, de modo que prevalece la última edición y no la lectura más lenta.

records.source: Qt aborts the process when a running QThread is destroyed, and a worker that delivers into a widget on its way out is a use-after-free. ``JobRunner.shutdown`` handles both.
records.translation: Qt aborta el proceso cuando se destruye un QThread en ejecución, y un proceso de trabajo que entrega resultados a un widget que está desapareciendo es un uso tras liberación. ``JobRunner.shutdown`` se ocupa de ambas cosas.

records.context: Not the only line of defence, deliberately, because it is not always reached: this editor is a child inside a settings panel, and navigating away from that panel destroys it without any close event. What covers that case is the runner itself — the QThreads are unparented and retire themselves, and ``JobRunner._relay`` catches the ``RuntimeError`` PySide6 raises when a worker settles after its runner's C++ half has gone.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.row_exclusion.RowExclusionEditor.closeEvent#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Not the only line of defence, deliberately, because it is not always reached: this editor is a child inside a settings panel, and navigating away from that panel destroys it without any close event. What covers that case is the runner itself — the QThreads are unparented and retire themselves, and ``JobRunner._relay`` catches the ``RuntimeError`` PySide6 raises when a worker settles after its runner's C++ half has gone.
records.translation: No es la única línea de defensa, deliberadamente, porque no siempre se llega a ella: este editor es un hijo dentro de un panel de ajustes, y salir de ese panel lo destruye sin ningún evento de cierre. Lo que cubre ese caso es el propio ejecutor — los QThreads no tienen padre y se retiran solos, y ``JobRunner._relay`` captura el ``RuntimeError`` que lanza PySide6 cuando un proceso de trabajo termina después de que haya desaparecido la mitad C++ de su ejecutor.

records.context: Usable means torch can reach it: a card spaCR cannot run on is not a compatible card however well the driver reports it. records.source: Usable means torch can reach it: a card spaCR cannot run on is not a compatible card however well the driver reports it. Torch is asked first for that reason, and NVML second because it names the card even when torch was built without CUDA -- which is the case worth telling apart, since the answer there is "install a CUDA build", not "buy a card".
records.translation: Utilizable significa que torch puede acceder a ella: una tarjeta en la que spaCR no puede ejecutarse no es una tarjeta compatible por bien que la notifique el controlador. Por eso se pregunta primero a Torch, y en segundo lugar a NVML, porque este nombra la tarjeta incluso cuando torch se compiló sin CUDA -- que es el caso que merece distinguirse, ya que la respuesta ahí es "install a CUDA build" (instalar una compilación con soporte), no "buy a card" (comprar una tarjeta).

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The engine is :mod:`spacr.gene_measurement_sweep`; this is a thin panel over it. The three corrections the sweep applies (identifiers excluded, Benjamini-Hochberg across the grid, circularity reported per row) live in the engine, so a settings CSV, a macro and this button apply them identically.
records.translation: El motor es :mod:`spacr.gene_measurement_sweep`; esto es un panel ligero sobre él. Las tres correcciones que aplica el barrido (identificadores excluidos, Benjamini-Hochberg sobre toda la cuadrícula, circularidad notificada por fila) están en el motor, de modo que un CSV de ajustes, una macro y este botón las aplican de forma idéntica.

records.source: The sweep runs off the GUI thread. Qt widgets built on a worker thread can crash the process, so the worker touches no widget and returns plain data, and the figure is rendered by matplotlib's Agg canvas, which owns no Qt object.
records.translation: El barrido se ejecuta fuera del hilo de la GUI. Los widgets de Qt construidos en un hilo de trabajo pueden hacer caer el proceso, así que el proceso de trabajo no toca ningún widget y devuelve datos simples, y la figura la representa el lienzo Agg de matplotlib, que no posee ningún objeto de Qt.

The mark drawing, the fixed categorical hue order, the density raster, the selection ring, the legend and the brush are one implementation, and a second one would be a second set of rules to keep in step with the first — the mistake :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pivot_builder` avoids by not drawing anything at all.
records.translation: :class:`TrellisCanvas` **hereda de** :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` en lugar de reimplementarlo. records.context: **the layout** comes from :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.trellis`, which knows about wrapping and about blank slots, rather than from ``facet_grid`` directly;
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_view#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **the layout** comes from :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.trellis`, which knows about wrapping and about blank slots, rather than from ``facet_grid`` directly;
records.translation: **la disposición** procede de :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.trellis`, que sabe de ajuste en filas y de huecos en blanco, en lugar de proceder directamente de ``facet_grid``;

records.context: **the scales are set per panel from that panel's own group**. Every panel's limits are written explicitly rather than left to matplotlib's ``sharex``: sharing makes panels agree with *each other*, but on whatever the first one autoscaled to, which is not necessarily wide enough for the rest. Under :data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.SCALE_SHARED` — the default — every panel is handed the identical tuple, which is a property a test can assert and an eye can trust.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_view#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **the scales are set per panel from that panel's own group**. Every panel's limits are written explicitly rather than left to matplotlib's ``sharex``: sharing makes panels agree with *each other*, but on whatever the first one autoscaled to, which is not necessarily wide enough for the rest. Under :data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.SCALE_SHARED` — the default — every panel is handed the identical tuple, which is a property a test can assert and an eye can trust.
records.translation: **las escalas se establecen por panel a partir del propio grupo de ese panel**. Los límites de cada panel se escriben explícitamente en lugar de dejarse al ``sharex`` de matplotlib: compartir hace que los paneles coincidan *entre sí*, pero con lo que el primero haya ajustado automáticamente, que no es necesariamente lo bastante amplio para el resto. Con :data:`~spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_spec.SCALE_SHARED` — el valor predeterminado — cada panel recibe la tupla idéntica, una propiedad que una prueba puede verificar y en la que el ojo puede confiar.

records.source: ``payload['frame']`` is optional: a DataFrame with one row per point, carrying whatever the caller measured. Without it the explorer can still identify its points (from the records' ``prcfo``) and so still publishes and receives selections — but a filter on a measurement column has nothing here to test, and is reported as ignored rather than silently drawing everything as if it had applied.
records.translation: ``payload['frame']`` es opcional: un DataFrame con una fila por punto que contiene lo que haya medido el llamador. Sin él, el explorador puede seguir identificando sus puntos (a partir del ``prcfo`` de los registros) y, por tanto, sigue publicando y recibiendo selecciones — pero un filtro sobre una columna de medidas no tiene nada que comprobar aquí, y se notifica como ignorado en lugar de dibujar en silencio todo como si se hubiera aplicado.
